samir_k: Hey, hitting an import error in CI after we switched to installing the SDK from our requirements.txt (git URL). Locally `pip install "redwood-sdk[httpx]"` works fine but CI fails when starting the app. We pin with a requirements.txt line:
```
git+https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk@v1.7.0#egg=redwood-sdk
```
When the app tries to initialize the client using the httpx transport we get: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/main.py", line 8, in <module>
    from redwood import RedwoodClient
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 2, in <module>
    from .transport.httpx import HttpxTransport
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'
```
I suspect extras weren't installed from the git URL. Any quick repro/CI fixes?

jessica_support: can you paste the CI `pip freeze` (inside the venv used by the job) and the exact requirements line? also which pip version in CI? :eyes:

ci-bot: [CI job output snippet attached] python 3.10, pip 23.2.1, wheel cache enabled

samir_k: here's pip freeze from the failing job:
```
redwood-sdk==1.7.0
uvicorn==0.20.0
# no httpx in the list
```
requirements line (exact):
```
git+https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk@v1.7.0#egg=redwood-sdk
```

jessica_support: yep, that explains it. When installing from a VCS URL you need to include extras explicitly. Two common ways that work in requirements.txt: 
1) PEP 508 direct URL (recommended):
```
redwood-sdk[httpx] @ git+https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk@v1.7.0
```
2) If you prefer the egg fragment, you must URL-encode the brackets so the parser preserves them: 
```
git+https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk@v1.7.0#egg=redwood-sdk%5Bhttpx%5D
```
Note: some CI runners/caches will store a wheel of the VCS install without extras if the extras weren't requested on first install, so you may need to clear the pip cache or the CI cache.

connie_engineering: adding that: also check for a constraints file in the pipeline that might pin httpx away or otherwise block resolution (constraints can prevent extras from being pulled). Quick reproduce commands in the job: 
```
python -c "import importlib, sys; print('httpx' in sys.modules, importlib.util.find_spec('httpx') is not None)"
pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
pip freeze | grep httpx || true
```

samir_k: thanks — I tried the PEP 508 form and re-ran the CI with caches flushed. Repro steps I used locally to validate:
```
# reproduce locally quickly
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install "redwood-sdk[httpx] @ git+https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk@v1.7.0"
python -c "import httpx; print(httpx.__version__)"
python -c "from redwood import RedwoodClient; print('ok')"
```
CI now passes and the import error is gone. :tada:

jessica_support: great! leaving note for docs team to add an example for VCS installs + extras. if anyone sees this pattern again, recommend switching to PEP 508 syntax in requirements and clearing caches.

samir_k: will do — thanks everyone!
